cards.text: World War II: The liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation continues. Bajina Bašta in western Serbia is among the liberated cities.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-51.
Sirimavo Bandaranaike is sworn in as prime minister of Ceylon, becoming the world's first democratically elected female head of government.
The United Kingdom recognizes Bahrain's independence, which is commemorated annually as Bahrain's National Day.
The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
Tonkin Campaign: French forces capture the Sơn Tây citadel.
Norwegians vote to end the union with Sweden.
United Arab Emirates holds its first-ever elections.
Erden Eruç completes the first solo human-powered circumnavigation of the world.
SS Valencia runs aground on rocks on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, killing more than 130.
William Gray of Hartford, Connecticut is granted United States Patent Number 408,709 for "Coin-controlled apparatus for telephones."
The passenger steamer SS Columbia sinks after colliding with the steam schooner San Pedro off Shelter Cove, California, killing 88 people.
A performance of Wagner's Das Rheingold opens the first Ring cycle at the first Bayreuth Festival.
Norwegians vote to end the union with Sweden.
Inauguration of Leopold I of Belgium, first king of the Belgians.
The Convention of London, a treaty between the United Kingdom and the United Netherlands, is signed in London, England.
The Chicago Bears defeat the Portsmouth Spartans in the first NFL playoff game to win the NFL Championship.
The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
Bonanza, the first regularly scheduled TV program presented in color, is launched in the United States.
World War II: The liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation continues. Bajina Bašta in western Serbia is among the liberated cities.
The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
The Nutcracker by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky premiers in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
World War II: Australian and American forces defeat Japanese army and navy units in the bitterly fought Battle of Buna–Gona.
Second Anglo-Sikh War: The Siege of Multan ends after nine months when the last Sikh defenders of Multan, Punjab, surrender.
A magnitude 7.0 earthquakes strikes off the coast of Taiwan, triggering a tsunami and killing at least 580 people.
Third Taiwan Strait Crisis: The People's Liberation Army begins firing missiles into the waters north of Taiwan.
Hurricane Gilbert devastates Jamaica; it turns towards Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula two days later, causing an estimated $5 billion in damage.
World War II: The liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation continues. Bajina Bašta in western Serbia is among the liberated cities.
Creation of the Central Intelligence Group, forerunner of the Central Intelligence Agency.
The Soviet Union launches a large rocket, Lunik II, at the Moon.
NS Savannah, the first nuclear-powered cargo-passenger ship, is launched as a showcase for Dwight D. Eisenhower's "Atoms for Peace" initiative.
World War II: Australian and American forces defeat Japanese army and navy units in the bitterly fought Battle of Buna–Gona.
Tonkin Campaign: French forces capture the Sơn Tây citadel.
World War I: Admiral Franz von Hipper commands a raid on Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby.
A Lockheed L-188 Electra crashes in Jamba, Cuando, Angola, killing 141 people.
Typhoon Maemi, the strongest recorded typhoon to strike South Korea, made landfall near Busan.
NASA launches into orbit the Terra platform carrying five Earth Observation instruments, including ASTER, CERES, MISR, MODIS and MOPITT.
World War II: The liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation continues. Bajina Bašta in western Serbia is among the liberated cities.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-51.
One hundred fifty-six Congolese Tutsi refugees are massacred at the Gatumba refugee camp in Burundi.
Sirimavo Bandaranaike is sworn in as prime minister of Ceylon, becoming the world's first democratically elected female head of government.
SS Valencia runs aground on rocks on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, killing more than 130.
The Haiyuan earthquake of 8.5Mw rocks the Gansu province in China, killing an estimated 200,000.
Israel–United Arab Emirates relations are formally established.
The Abundant Life Christian School shooting in Madison, Wisconsin, United States, takes place, resulting in the death of three people.
Félicette, a black and white female Parisian stray cat, becomes the first cat launched into space.
World War II: Soviet Union begins the liberation of Czechoslovakia from Nazi Germany.
World War II: The state funeral of Field Marshal Erwin Rommel takes place in Ulm, Germany.
First Balkan War: King Peter I of Serbia issues a declaration "To the Serbian People", as his country joins the war.
Texas Instruments announces the Regency TR-1, the first mass-produced transistor radio.
Count Bernhard von Bülow becomes chancellor of Germany.
Johannes Brahms conducts the premiere of his Double Concerto, composed for violinist Joseph Joachim and cellist Robert Hausmann.
The Supreme Council of Azerbaijan adopts a declaration of independence from the Soviet Union.
Merpati Nustantara Airlines Flight 5601 crashes into Mount Papandayan near the town of Garut in West Java, Indonesia, killing 31.
Argentine military officer and politician Juan Perón marries actress Eva Duarte.
The Crimean Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic is formed as part of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic.
Count Bernhard von Bülow becomes chancellor of Germany.
The USSR's nuclear program receives plans for the United States plutonium bomb from Klaus Fuchs at the Los Alamos National Laboratory.
The United States takes possession of Puerto Rico from Spain.
The Second Opium War finally ends at the Convention of Peking with the ratification of the Treaty of Tientsin, an unequal treaty.
Herman Melville's Moby-Dick is first published as The Whale by Richard Bentley of London.
Based on the world's first children's art museum, the Henrik Igityan National Centre for Aesthetics opens in Yerevan.
The Soviet probe Venera 4 reaches Venus and becomes the first spacecraft to measure the atmosphere of another planet.

anchor.name: Beatrice Worsley
anchor.description: First female computer scientist in Canada

cards.text: The USSR's nuclear program receives plans for the United States plutonium bomb from Klaus Fuchs at the Los Alamos National Laboratory.
The Soviet probe Venera 4 reaches Venus and becomes the first spacecraft to measure the atmosphere of another planet.
World War II: The state funeral of Field Marshal Erwin Rommel takes place in Ulm, Germany.
World War II: Soviet Union begins the liberation of Czechoslovakia from Nazi Germany.
Félicette, a black and white female Parisian stray cat, becomes the first cat launched into space.
The United States takes possession of Puerto Rico from Spain.
First Balkan War: King Peter I of Serbia issues a declaration "To the Serbian People", as his country joins the war.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) begins allowing people to have home satellite earth stations without a federal government license.
The Supreme Council of Azerbaijan adopts a declaration of independence from the Soviet Union.
King Otto of Bavaria is deposed by his cousin, Prince Regent Ludwig, who assumes the title Ludwig III.
In Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co. the Supreme Court of the United States declares unapportioned income tax to be unconstitutional.
Women's suffrage in the United States: In defiance of the law, suffragist Susan B. Anthony votes for the first time, and is later fined $100.
World War I: France and the British Empire declare war on the Ottoman Empire.
The Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act, establishing the United States Civil Service, is enacted by Congress.
Westward expansion of the United States: John C. Frémont is appointed Governor of the new California Territory.
The first Mormon pioneers make their exodus from Nauvoo, Illinois, westward towards Salt Lake Valley.
World War II: The British armed merchant cruiser HMS Jervis Bay is sunk by the German pocket battleship Admiral Scheer.
World War II: Santo Tomas Internment Camp is liberated from Japanese authority.
Future abolitionist Frederick Douglass escapes from slavery.
Time zone: New Zealand officially adopts a standard time to be observed nationally.
American Civil War: Confederate General Leonidas Polk invades neutral Kentucky, prompting the state legislature to ask for Union assistance.
First ascent of Aletschhorn, second summit of the Bernese Alps.
Konstantinos Kanaris blows up the Ottoman navy's flagship at Chios, killing the Kapudan Pasha Nasuhzade Ali Pasha.
American Revolutionary War: The British Army abandons Philadelphia.
Joseph Whidbey leads an expedition to search for the Northwest Passage near Juneau, Alaska.
Italian anarchist Michele Angiolillo assassinates Spanish Prime Minister Antonio Cánovas del Castillo.
North Dakota and South Dakota are admitted as the 39th and 40th U.S. states.
The Rome General Peace Accords end a 16-year civil war in Mozambique.
NASA's Phoenix lander touches down in the Green Valley region of Mars to search for environments suitable for water and microbial life.
Hurricane Flora kills 6,000 in Cuba and Haiti.
The law on same-sex marriage comes into force in South Africa, legalizing same-sex marriage for the first time on the African continent.
SpaceShipOne wins the Ansari X Prize for private spaceflight.
The Doom Bar in Cornwall claims two ships, Island Maid and Angele, the latter killing the entire crew except the captain.
World War I: An explosion kills more than 100 people and destroys a Shell Loading Plant in New Jersey.
Oprah Winfrey airs her last show, ending her 25-year run of The Oprah Winfrey Show.
Prime Minister Modi of India inaugurates the 2nd Space Port of India - Kulasekarapattinam Spaceport.
A German officer is killed in Bucharest, Romania, sparking a rebellion and pogrom by the Iron Guard, killing 125 Jews and 30 soldiers.
The Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia is declared.
The Beatles' last public performance, on the roof of Apple Records in London. The impromptu concert is broken up by the police.
The Holocaust: In Berlin, the Gestapo arrest 1,800 Jewish men with German wives, leading to the Rosenstrasse protest.
Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet survives an assassination attempt by the FPMR; five of Pinochet's bodyguards are killed.
The United States takes possession of Puerto Rico from Spain.
The Boxer Rebellion in Qing dynasty (modern-day China) officially ends with the signing of the Boxer Protocol.
Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump begins.
Two trains collide south of the Vale of Tempe in Greece, leading to the deaths of at least 57 people and leaving 58 missing and 85 injured.
Somalia and Ethiopia sign a truce to end the Ethio-Somali War.
The United States annexes the Kingman Reef.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-52 to deploy the LAGEOS-2 satellite and microgravity experiments.
Racially motivated Nihon Shōgakkō fire lit by a serial arsonist kills 10 children in Sacramento, California.
After Egypt gains nominal independence from the United Kingdom, Fuad I becomes King of Egypt.
Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) is established as a public company in Germany.
Women enlist in the United States Marine Corps for the first time. Opha May Johnson is the first woman to enlist.
Stockpiles of obsolete ammunition explode at an ex-military ammunition depot in the village of Gërdec, Albania, killing 26 people.
NASA announces that the ALH 84001 meteorite, thought to originate from Mars, contains evidence of primitive life-forms.

anchor.name: Fred Shero
anchor.description: Canadian former ice hockey player and coach (1925–1990)

cards.text: South African Airways Flight 295 crashes into the Indian Ocean, killing all 159 people on board.
The people of the Saar region vote in a referendum to unite with West Germany instead of France.
The Central Intelligence Agency releases documents under the Freedom of Information Act revealing it had engaged in mind-control experiments.
Holocaust: Fifteen hundred Jews from Pidhaytsi are sent by Nazis to Bełżec extermination camp.
The Grand Ole Opry begins broadcasting in Nashville, Tennessee, as the WSM Barn Dance.
World War I: Serbia declares war on Germany; Austria declares war on Russia.
The Communist Party of Australia is founded in Sydney.
The fully restored USS Constitution (a.k.a. Old Ironsides) celebrates its 200th birthday by setting sail for the first time in 116 years.
The Russian parliament approves the name change of Leningrad back to Saint Petersburg. The change is effective October 1.
Spanish Civil War: An Armed Forces rebellion against the recently elected leftist Popular Front government of Spain starts the civil war.
The Homestead Strike begins near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
The Council of Europe is founded following a speech by Winston Churchill at the University of Zurich.
Charles J. Guiteau is hanged in Washington, D.C. for the assassination of U.S. President James Garfield.
The first hydropower plant of Finland is commissioned along the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, Pirkanmaa.
Vega becomes the first star (other than the Sun) to be photographed.
Richard Wagner's Siegfried, the penultimate opera in his Ring cycle, is premiered at the Bayreuth Festspielhaus.
SpaceShipOne, piloted by Brian Binnie, makes its first powered and first supersonic flight.
The Solomon Islands join the United Nations.
Opening of the first German National Assembly (Nationalversammlung) in Frankfurt, Germany.
Lewis and Clark Expedition: Scouting ahead of the expedition, Meriwether Lewis and four companions sight the Great Falls of the Missouri River.
The American League of Colored Laborers, the first African American labor union in the United States, is established in New York City.
Louis-Alexandre Berthier removes Pope Pius VI from power.
The Disruption in Edinburgh of the Free Church of Scotland from the Church of Scotland.
The Seven Years' War begins when Great Britain declares war on France.
George Frideric Handel's oratorio Messiah makes its world premiere in Dublin, Ireland.
The American adventurer William Walker conquers Nicaragua.
The USS Jeannette is crushed in an Arctic Ocean ice pack.
